notes: NWC definition used for historical: Non-cash working capital = (Total current assets - cash & cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - notes payable and current maturities of long-term debt). This produces negative working capital values for RSG based on balance sheet structure; your pipeline may use a different operating working capital definition, so reconcile accordingly.

EBIT definition used: GAAP operating income from the consolidated statement of income (not adjusted EBITDA; does not add back interest/taxes). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

D&A driver used: GAAP 'Depreciation, depletion and amortization' (excludes 'accretion' which is a separate income-statement line). This intentionally keeps D&A consistent with the historical income statement line item but differs from Republic’s guidance presentation that includes accretion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Tax rate input: effective tax rate estimated from (Provision for income taxes) / (Income before income taxes) averaged across FY2023-2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

NOL balance: set using deferred tax asset 'Net operating loss carryforwards' tax-effect amount of $60M from the deferred tax footnote; Republic also mentions an estimated tax effect of $51M for state NOLs, so the balance is a modeled proxy. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Comps multiples: EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E NTM were not populated because forward EV/NTM revenue/EBITDA and forward P/E were not available from the accessible free sources used in this run; peers are listed for model completeness.

catalysts: Potential 2026 guidance upside/downside driven by realized average yield vs. management’s assumed ranges and changes in volume. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))

Recycling commodity price moves and policy-related impacts could shift operating income (management highlights sensitivity to recycling commodity pricing). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Execution on technology/process improvements (dispatch, fleet maintenance, recycling contamination reduction) could support incremental margin and productivity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Continued capital return (repurchases/dividends) could support per-share results if the company sustains free cash flow. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))
company_overview: Republic Services is one of the largest providers of environmental services in North America, operating across the U.S. and Canada with collection, transfer, recycling, and landfill operations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

The company operates an integrated platform spanning collection operations, transfer stations, recycling centers, and active landfills, supporting internalization and durable service relationships. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Revenue is primarily driven by pricing (average yield/core price) plus volumes across collection and disposal-related lines of business. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))
current_context: FY2025 revenue was $16.591B (GAAP), with operating income (EBIT) of $3.302B; adjusted EBITDA was $5.307B (32.0% margin). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

2026 guidance calls for revenue of $17.050B to $17.150B and adjusted EBITDA of $5.475B to $5.525B, reflecting expected average yield growth and volume decline assumptions. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))

As of Dec 31, 2025, remaining share repurchase authorization capacity was approximately $1.7B. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored to management’s 2026 revenue guidance (pricing-led yield growth with modest volume drag) and then extends with conservative mid-single-digit dynamics. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))

EBIT margins are modeled to mean-revert with slight long-run expansion, consistent with historical operating income margin levels and ongoing cost management. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity and depreciation are kept tied to historical spend (property/equipment purchases) and historical depreciation intensity, supporting stable reinvestment assumptions in the DCF. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Working capital is modeled as persistently negative (typical for waste haulers/disposal networks), with modest improvement in the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Operational resilience is supported by internalization: management reported ~67% of collected volume disposed at owned/operated landfills in 2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Commodity price volatility can affect both revenue and operating income; Republic quantified a sensitivity for recycling commodity price changes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Cost inflation (labor, fuel/diesel) and disruptions could pressure margins relative to the base case. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))

Environmental liabilities and regulatory compliance requirements could increase operating costs or capital expenditures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Higher interest rates/credit spreads can increase financing costs, particularly given floating-rate exposure discussed in the filing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

presentation.subtitle: Republic Services (RSG) — DCF + Peer Inputs (Valuation Model Package)
valuation_summary: DCF base case uses GAAP operating income (EBIT) and depreciation drivers from Republic’s SEC filings, with conservative operating leverage assumptions and economically sensible terminal growth (2.0%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Scenario sets (bull/bear) adjust only growth/margins and discount/terminal parameters to reflect a plausible range around guidance and cost/volume sensitivity, rather than promotional swings. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/republic-services-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-provides-2026-full-year-financial-guidance-302689912.html))

Capital expenditures are tied to historical purchases of property and equipment, ensuring reinvestment levels remain consistent with the company’s asset-heavy platform. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))

Net debt inputs use Dec 31, 2025 cash (cash & equivalents) and debt from the balance sheet; restricted cash is excluded from the ‘cash’ field to avoid double counting. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060391/000106039126000094/rsg-20251231.htm))
